headline: High risk: Cursor’s broad filesystem/network/MCP and auto-run shell can amplify prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors when paired with a non-runnable docs-only NLP list.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests clipboard, workspace files, and MCP content, so attacker-controlled text can reach its agent loop. awesome-nlp is a docs-only, non-runnable list with no isolation or parser details, so the pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly evidenced. The interaction exists in default Cursor workflows, but the blast radius is mainly instruction hijack rather than guaranteed system compromise.
conditions: IF content from awesome-nlp is copied into Cursor chat or opened as a file, THEN prompt-like text can influence Cursor's agent loop.
IF Cursor reads MCP or workspace content without provenance checks, THEN injected instructions may be followed.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-driven ingestion for untrusted text.
Keep awesome-nlp content in read-only notes, not active Cursor buffers.
Turn off MCP servers for the session.
Use a separate workspace for untrusted content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches open files, workspace files, clipboard contents, and sends data to external model providers/MCP servers by default. awesome-nlp itself is a docs-only repository, so the main leakage path is from user data in Cursor rather than from the list; however, the pair still creates a shared handling surface where copied or opened sensitive material can be transmitted outward.
conditions: IF sensitive text is opened or pasted into Cursor while model calls are enabled, THEN that content can leave the local machine.
IF workspace files from the awesome-nlp context contain secrets and are opened in Cursor, THEN they may be uploaded to inference backends.
mitigations: Avoid pasting secrets into Cursor.
Close sensitive files before invoking the agent.
Disable model-provider calls for the session.
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before outbound requests.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress; awesome-nlp is non-runnable and contributes no locking or coordination. In default Cursor workflows, concurrent edits through shared local filesystem state can collide with other instances or manual edits, and git state changes can be overwritten or conflicted. The pair lacks any documented coordination primitive, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF two Cursor instances edit the same workspace, THEN file and git conflicts can occur.
IF the user manually edits files while Cursor is running, THEN last-writer-wins overwrites are possible.
mitigations: Use one editor instance per workspace.
Pause Cursor before manual bulk edits.
Commit or stash before agent-driven changes.
Restrict the session to a throwaway branch.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can act on its own outputs via shell and git tools, while awesome-nlp provides only a static list with no verification layer. That makes it plausible for generated suggestions or copied snippets to be treated as authoritative and then turned into edits or commands. The blast radius is multiple work products, but not inherently irreversible without extra user action.
conditions: IF Cursor uses text from awesome-nlp as source material for code or commands, THEN errors can propagate into edits or shell actions.
IF the user approves auto-generated commands, THEN mistaken outputs can cascade into repository changes.
mitigations: Require manual review before command approval.
Cross-check generated facts against primary sources.
Limit the agent to read-only mode for research tasks.
Review diffs before commit.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class is identified in awesome-nlp, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch to cite against it. Cursor does handle clipboard contents and sends data to external providers, which can matter if regulated data is introduced, but that scenario is not established by the profiles. The other agent is not cited because the compliance risk is not pair-specific here.
conditions: IF regulated data is pasted into Cursor, THEN outbound processing may create a compliance issue.
IF the workspace contains data subject to retention or residency rules, THEN Cursor's external calls may conflict with policy.
mitigations: Do not use regulated data in this workspace.
Disable external model calls for regulated tasks.
Separate compliant and non-compliant projects.
Review retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls.
